name: Medibank OSHC Team
subject: ⚠ YOUR COVER HAS EXPIRED!!!
body: Your Overseas Student Health Cover has EXPIRED. Renew within 2 hours or your visa may be cancelled.

flags.greeting: Generic greeting. Medibank knows your name
flags.body: Threats and a 2-hour deadline are pressure tactics
flags.link: The real domain is medibank-oshc-renew.xyz, not medibank.com.au

tip: Real insurers never threaten visa cancellation by email.

name: Medibank Rebates
subject: Health Rebate Available
body: A rebate of $1,284 is ready for you. Claim within 24 hours or it will expire.

flags.body: Unexpected money plus a 24-hour deadline is a classic lure

tip: Unexpected rebates are bait. Check your Medibank account directly.

name: Medibank
subject: Welcome to your OSHC membership
body: Your membership is set up. You can view your cover details in your Medibank account or app.
tip: Neutral emails with an official domain are usually fine.
why: Official medibank.com.au domain, personal greeting, no threats, no requests for credentials.

name: Medibank Security
subject: Urgent Login Alert
body: Suspicious activity detected on your Medibank account. Verify now to avoid suspension.
tip: Hyphenated brand names are a warning sign.

name: Medibank
subject: New features in the Medibank app
body: We've added a few updates to the app, including easier access to your digital membership card.
tip: Marketing emails can be real. Check domain and demands.
why: Official medibank.com.au domain, harmless content, no credential request.

name: Medibank Rewards
subject: 🎉 You've WON a $1,000 gift card!
body: You were randomly selected as a Medibank member! Enter your card details to receive your prize today.

flags.sender: A random '.top' domain is not Medibank
flags.body: You can't win a contest you never entered, and prizes never need card details
flags.link: Prize site collects your card details

tip: If it sounds too good to be true, it is.

name: Medibank Claims
subject: Your OSHC refund of $246.80 is pending
body: Your recent claim was overpaid. Confirm your bank details to receive your refund.

flags.body: Real refunds go to details already on file, not via email links
flags.link: Subdomain trick: the real domain is secure-refund.net

tip: Read a domain right to left from the first single '/'.

name: Medibank
subject: Your OSHC claim has been processed
body: Your claim from 12 March has been processed. View the details in your Medibank account or app.
tip: Real emails tell you what happened without demanding data.
why: Official medibank.com.au domain, personal greeting, no urgency, no data requests.

name: Medibank Visa Compliance
subject: Visa health cover under review – action required
body: Your student visa health cover is under review. Upload a photo of your passport and bank statement within 24 hours.

flags.greeting: Generic greeting for a personal cover matter
flags.body: Passport and bank documents plus a 24-hour deadline
flags.link: medibank-visa-check.com is a lookalike, not medibank.com.au

tip: Insurers don't ask for passport or bank documents through email links.

name: Medibank Payments
subject: Payment failed – update your card today
body: Your last OSHC premium payment failed. Update your card today or your cover will be suspended.

flags.sender: A free webmail address for a big insurer
flags.body: Threat of suspension and a same-day deadline are pressure tactics
flags.link: Payment page on an unrelated '.top' domain

tip: Check payment issues by logging in to the app yourself.

name: Medibank
subject: Your OSHC statement is ready
body: Your latest statement is available. Sign in to your Medibank account or app to view it.
tip: Real emails point you to the official site or app, not a form.
why: Sender and link both belong to medibank.com.au; the tone is calm and informational.

name: Medibank
subject: Your premium payment receipt
body: Thanks for your payment of $42.50. No action is needed.
tip: 'No action needed' is a good sign.
why: Official domain, receipt only, nothing to click or enter.

name: Medibank OSHC
subject: Priya, your OSHC cover ends 31 December
body: To keep your cover active, please confirm your details by 31 Dec. It only takes a minute.

flags.link: The '@' trick: everything before '@' is ignored. You land on verify-oshc-members.net

tip: Spear-phishing uses your name. Always check the real domain.

name: Medibank Member Support
subject: Your Medibank password expires in 3 days
body: Your Medibank online password expires soon. Sign in to keep access to your claims and membership card.

flags.link: Subdomain trick: the real domain is member-portal.net

tip: Go to the app or site yourself instead of clicking.

name: Medibank
subject: Your OSHC card is ready
body: Your digital card is ready in the Medibank app. Your cover renews on 31 December. No action is needed unless your details changed.
tip: A date isn't a threat. Look for pressure and requests.
why: Official domain, mentions a date but with no pressure, no request for credentials.

name: Sarah Nguyen, Medibank Claims
subject: Claim review – please see document
body: I've reviewed your claim. The outcome is in a shared document. Sign in with your Google account to open it.

flags.body: Asks you to sign in with your account to read a document
flags.link: Looks like Google Docs but the real domain is medibank-docs.cc

tip: Even a named staff member can be spoofed. Check your Medibank account instead.

name: Medibank
subject: Your contact details were updated
body: You updated your address on 5 May. If this wasn't you, call the number on the back of your membership card.
tip: A security notice that points you to a number you already have is normal.
why: Official domain, calm confirmation of a change, no link asking for credentials.

name: Medibank Claims
subject: Claim rejected – appeal within 12 hours
body: Your claim #48213 was rejected due to a missing document. Appeal within 12 hours or the claim will lapse.

flags.body: A 12-hour deadline to push you into acting

tip: Zoom in on letters: 'rn' looks like 'm'.
